value.deck: A popular security tool got an update to help developers catch hidden safety flaws in their software before hackers can exploit them.
shortVersion: Software powers many tools we use daily, so keeping it safe from hackers is crucial. A security tool called CodeQL acts like a digital inspector that checks software code for hidden flaws.
A new update, CodeQL 2.26.3, improves how the tool inspects web code and automated software building steps. This helps developers catch security problems much earlier while they work.
Catching these flaws early protects public software projects from cyber attacks. This keeps the everyday programs that rely on those building blocks safer for everyone.
value.plainLanguage: A tool that scans code for security flaws received an update to help developers catch safety weaknesses earlier in popular programming tools.

keyTerms.meaning: A security tool that automatically scans code to find safety flaws before software is released.
Automated instructions that help developers build, test, and publish their software automatically.
A weakness or flaw in software that could allow hackers to cause harm.

value.whyItMatters: When public software building blocks are secure, the apps and websites you use every day are much safer from cyber attacks.
watchNext: Watch to see if software teams adopt these improved security checks in their daily work.
Look out for future updates that add security checks for other popular programming languages.
